'''Carrick Felix''' (born August 17, 1990) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played three years of [[college basketball]] for [[Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball|Arizona State]] before being drafted by the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] with the 33rd overall pick in the [[2013 NBA draft]].<ref name="draft">{{cite web |last=Adams |first=Nick |date=June 27, 2013 |title=Cavaliers Select Bennett and Karasev in the first round of the 2013 NBA Draft |url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/bennett-karasav-130627 |accessdate=December 1, 2023 |work=NBA.com}}</ref>

==High school career==
Born in [[Las Vegas, Nevada]], Felix played high school basketball at [[Millennium High School (Goodyear, Arizona)|Millennium High School]] in [[Goodyear, Arizona]]. During his senior season at Millennium, Felix led his team to a state championship and was named MVP of the state championship. As a senior in 2007–08, he averaged 19.7 points, 13.2 rebounds and 1.5 steals per game.<ref>{{cite web |title=Carrick Felix - 2009-10 Men's Basketball |url=https://athletics.csi.edu/sports/mens-basketball/roster/carrick-felix/96 |accessdate=December 1, 2023 |work=CSI.edu}}</ref>

==College career==
After [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirting]] the 2008–09 season for medical reasons, Felix averaged 14.8 points and 4.7 rebounds in 2009–10 at [[College of Southern Idaho]].<ref name=arizona_bio>{{cite web|title=Carrick Felix Bio|url=http://www.thesundevils.com/ViewArticle.dbml?&DB_OEM_ID=30300&ATCLID=208247337|work=TheSunDevils.com|accessdate=October 22, 2013}}</ref> Felix joined the [[Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball|Arizona State Sun Devils]] for his final three years of eligibility. During his first year at Arizona State, Felix made appearances in 30 of the Sun Devils 31 games, averaging 14.5 minutes and 4.6 points and 1.6 rebounds per game. In his second season, he saw an increase in minutes up from 14.5 the previous season to 32.9 per game. He subsequently averaged 10.5 points and 4.0 rebounds per game.<ref name="arizona_bio"/> In his third and final year at Arizona State, Felix led the team, as a shooting guard, in rebounds per game with 8.1 and was second on the team in scoring with 14.6 points. He also led the entire Pac-12 with 13 double doubles. He was named second-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] and Pac-12 All-Defensive Team. He was also named the Pac-12 Scholar Athlete of the Year and earned first-team All-Pac-12 Academic Team honors.<ref name="arizona_bio"/>

==Professional career==
Felix was selected with the 33rd overall pick in the [[2013 NBA draft]] by the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref name="draft"/> On August 20, 2013, he signed with the Cavaliers.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/draft-picks-130820 Cavaliers Sign 2013 Draft Picks to Contracts]</ref> During his rookie season, he had multiple assignments to the [[Canton Charge]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/assignments_2013_14.html 2013-14 NBA Assignments] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140703151241/http://www.nba.com/dleague/assignments_2013_14.html |date=July 3, 2014 }}</ref>

On July 22, 2014, Felix was traded, along with a [[2015 NBA draft|2015]] second-round draft pick and cash considerations, to the [[Utah Jazz]] in exchange for [[John Lucas III]], [[Malcolm Thomas (basketball, born 1988)|Malcolm Thomas]] and [[Erik Murphy]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 22, 2014 |title=Jazz Acquires Carrick Felix and Draft Pick |url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-acquires-carrick-felix-and-draft-pick |access-date=December 1, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On October 27, 2014, he was waived by the Jazz.<ref>{{cite news |date=October 27, 2014 |title=Jazz Waive Felix |work=NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-waive-felix |accessdate=December 1, 2023}}</ref> On November 1, 2014, he was selected by the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] with the fourth overall pick in the [[2014 NBA Development League Draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/santacruz/warriors_select_7.html |title=Santa Cruz Warriors Select 7 Players in the 2014 NBA D-League Draft |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2014-11-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141104183613/http://www.nba.com/dleague/santacruz/warriors_select_7.html |archive-date=2014-11-04 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On December 4, 2014, he was waived by the Warriors after sustaining a left knee injury.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 4, 2014 |title=Santa Cruz Warriors Sign Dominique Sutton |url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/santa-cruz-warriors-sign-dominique-sutton/n-4901592 |access-date=December 1, 2023 |website=oursportscentral.com}}</ref> Having "broke his left knee in half", Felix needed two surgeries and was told by multiple doctors his sporting career was over.<ref name=knee-injury>{{cite web|last=Ward|first=Roy|url=http://www.smh.com.au/sport/basketball/how-melbourne-united-import-carrick-felix-overcame-a-career-threatening-knee-injury-20171229-h0bb2y.html|title=How Melbourne United import Carrick Felix overcame a career threatening knee injury|work=SMH.com.au|date=December 29, 2017|accessdate=December 29, 2017}}</ref> He spent two years away from the game as a result.<ref name="knee-injury"/>

On November 1, 2016, Felix was acquired by the [[Long Island Nets]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Landstrom |first=A. |date=November 1, 2016 |title=Long Island Nets Announce Training Camp Roster |url=http://longisland.dleague.nba.com/news/long-island-nets-announce-training-camp-roster/ |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20161104000317/http://longisland.dleague.nba.com/news/long-island-nets-announce-training-camp-roster/ |archivedate=November 4, 2016 |accessdate=November 20, 2016 |work=NBA.com}}</ref>

After spending preseason with the [[Washington Wizards]], Felix signed with [[Melbourne United]] on December 22, 2017, as an injury replacement for [[Casey Prather]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Ward|first=Roy|url=http://www.smh.com.au/sport/basketball/melbourne-united-sign-recent-nba-player-carrick-felix-as-injury-replacement-20171222-h09iv1.html|title=Melbourne United sign recent NBA player Carrick Felix as injury replacement|work=SMH.com.au|date=December 22, 2017|accessdate=December 22, 2017}}</ref> Felix was removed from Melbourne's active roster on February 16, 2018, following Prather's return from injury.<ref>{{cite web |date=February 16, 2018 |title=Prather in, Felix out for Melbourne United |url=http://www.nbl.com.au/news/article/40241-prather-to-return-against-perth |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180216204554/http://www.nbl.com.au/news/article/40241-prather-to-return-against-perth |url-status=dead |archive-date=February 16, 2018 |accessdate=February 16, 2018 |work=NBL.com.au}}</ref> He remained with the team for their championship run.<ref name=summer-league>{{cite web|last=Santamaria|first=Liam|url=http://www.nbl.com.au/news/article/42585-washington-wizards-add-carrick-felix-for-summer-league|title=Washington Wizards add Carrick Felix for Summer League|work=NBL.com.au|date=June 23, 2018|accessdate=June 23, 2018}}</ref>

In June 2018, Felix re-joined the Wizards for the [[2018 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Santamaria |first=Liam |date=26 June 2018 |title=Washington Wizards add Carrick Felix for NBA Summer League |url=https://www.melbourneutd.com.au/news/article/washington-wizards-add-carrick-felix-for-nba-summer-league |access-date=23 October 2021 |website=melbourneutd.com.au}}</ref>

==Personal==
In his two years away from the game of basketball between 2014 and 2016, Felix created a mobile app called ZGNIT, which helps holiday makers book adventure equipments such as jet skis.<ref name="knee-injury"/>
